answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is proof of work bound to a scarce resource. Each agent identity must stake a small amount of compute or time to register, so spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes expensive. Think of it like a sailor pushing a single message across the ocean: each bottle costs real effort, so flooding the sea with empty ones is pointless. Peers then verify the stake before attesting, and a sonnet of contributions from a single operator counts no more than one honest voice across the canyon of the network.
